subject: Request: carveout for customer-controlled WAN jitter (Pegasus Analytics)
messages:
From: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@pegasus-analytics.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.lin@pegasus-analytics.com, noc@pegasus-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Observed tail-latency spikes + carveout request for private VPC

Hi Olga,

We rolled Redwood Private into our staging VPC last week and have been running representative traffic. Over the last three days we observed intermittent 200-400ms token-level tail spikes during model warmups. Our NOC traced the spikes to a customer-managed transit hop between our MPLS edge and the colo peer (see attached .pcap snippet).

Because this hop is under our control (managed by our WAN provider), we need to request a specific SLA carveout for WAN-induced jitter that attributes sub-500ms tail events to Pegasus when evident in net traces. Practically, we are asking Redwood to:
- Accept attribution to customer-managed WAN for latency variance when supported by packet captures and datacenter timestamps,
- Exclude those events from SLA credit calculations, and
- Define a joint evidence protocol (packet captures, SYN/ACK timing, and service-level synthetic tests).

Can we get an initial confirmation whether Redwood would accept this limited carveout and, if so, what evidence you would require? We can provide longer pcap captures and our WAN provider report.

Thanks,
Bryan
VP of Infrastructure
Pegasus Analytics

Attachments: pegasus_network_trace_20280820.pcap (excerpt)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@pegasus-analytics.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 25 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed tail-latency spikes + carveout request for private VPC

Hi Bryan — thanks for sending the trace and context.

Short answer: we are open to a narrowly-scoped attribution carveout tied to customer-controlled WAN faults, provided there is reproducible evidence and clear operational guardrails. Before we draft language, two quick asks:
1) Can you share a 24-hour packet capture window and the timestamps for the model inference requests (UTC)?
2) Would Pegasus be comfortable with a secondary verification step where Redwood runs a synthetic probe from the colo peer to your edge during a maintenance window?

From Redwood's side, our legal and SRE teams will want the carveout to be limited to:
- Latency/availability deviations demonstrably caused by customer-side transit,
- Events where packet-level causality is clear (no ambiguous multi-hop congestion), and
- A maximum time-limited amendment (e.g., reviewed quarterly).

I copied Marcus (SRE lead) and Naomi (Legal) to help scope the evidence protocol. Marcus — can you review the attached pcap and propose the minimum telemetry fields we need to accept attribution?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference

On attachments: thanks — got the pcap excerpt.

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 26 Aug 2028 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed tail-latency spikes + carveout request for private VPC

TL;DR: Acceptable if evidence meets our causality checklist.

Olga / Naomi — I pulled the pcap and the top-level notes: we see clear inter-arrival jitter at the edge for the affected flows, and the colo timestamps show queuing between hop 3 -> hop 4. That points to customer-side transit, but we need an evidence checklist to avoid gray-area disputes. Proposed minimum evidence items:
- Full TCP packet capture (pcap) for a 24-hour window in both directions, with synchronized timestamps (NTP-synced),
- Inference request IDs and their epoch timestamps (UTC) so we can map tokens to packets,
- Router hop lists/traceroutes from your edge to our colo at the same time windows,
- WAN provider incident ticket IDs if available, and
- Optional: jitter and loss graphs from your provider (1s resolution preferred).

Operationally, we recommend a gated workflow:
1) Pegasus delivers evidence bundle to a shared S3 bucket
2) Redwood SRE validates causality within five business days
3) If validated, the event is excluded from SLA crediting and a short remediation note is added to the incident log

We also want a limited carveout clause: attribution allowed up to 12 months and subject to quarterly review. If Pegasus prefers an ongoing carveout, we can draft higher-level operational SLAs (synthetic test pass rates) instead.

I'll draft a technical bullet list for the amendment and pass to Naomi for legal review.

—Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Aug 2028 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed tail-latency spikes + carveout request for private VPC

Folks — legal framing + minimal contract language suggestions below. Keep it tight: we do not want a blanket exclusion. Proposed legal text (high-level):

"Customer WAN Attribution Carveout: Redwood shall exclude from SLA credit calculations any latency or availability deviations that Redwood's SRE team reasonably attributes to Customer-managed WAN or transit components, provided Customer delivers (i) synchronized packet captures, (ii) inference request identifiers and timestamps, and (iii) corroborating network provider incident logs demonstrating fault or congestion within the Customer's network. Attribution determination shall be made within five (5) business days of evidence delivery and shall be applied retroactively to the specific validated events only. This carveout shall be reviewed quarterly and may be adjusted or revoked upon mutual notice."

Key negotiation levers: evidence window length, time to validate, whether the carveout auto-renews. Also flag: DocuSign or amendment should explicitly limit the carveout to token-latency attribution (not to uptime exclusions >30 minutes unless proven).

If agreeable, I can convert to redline-ready language and circulate to Pegasus with the technical checklist Marcus drafted.

—Naomi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@pegasus-analytics.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Aug 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: limited WAN-attribution carveout + next steps

Bryan — thanks for the quick turn. We've prepared a proposal that narrows the carveout to packet-proven customer transit faults and a short evidence protocol. Highlights:
- Attribution criteria: synchronized pcaps + request IDs + provider logs (Marcus's checklist attached),
- Validation SLA: Redwood will validate within 5 business days of evidence delivery,
- Scope: applies only to token latency tail events (per-request token latency spikes <= 12 hours total aggregated per incident); outages >30 minutes require additional proof and are not automatically excluded,
- Term: initial 3-month carveout with quarterly review; amendment auto-terminates unless both parties sign an extension,
- Operational hookup: Pegasus to provision an S3 bucket with read access for Redwood SRE; Redwood will provide a short-runbook for evidence handoff.

Attached: proposed-carveout-draft_v3.pdf
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/DEAL-9482-AMP
